events.title: Where will 2026 rank among the hottest years on record?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the numerical rank of how hot 2026 is when compared against all other years for which the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index has data.

Years will be ranked in descending order, starting with the hottest as number 1, the second hottest as number 2, etc.

If 2026 ties with any other year, it will resolve according to the place the year it ties with occupies.

This market will resolve immediately once the specified data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for the relevant years is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2026" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2026 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Strengthening El Niño conditions in the tropical Pacific, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +2°C in key regions by July 2026 and models projecting a very strong event through winter, represent the main driver elevating 2026’s implied odds for first- or second-warmest status. This natural variability overlays the long-term anthropogenic warming trend, pushing January–June global temperatures to the third-highest on record per NOAA while June ranked second-warmest. Berkeley Earth and Carbon Brief analyses tie the event’s lagged warming influence to a likely 1–2 ranking, with annual averages projected near or above 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Traders appear to weigh the intensifying El Niño more heavily than some statistical outlooks, assigning 65.5% probability to first place amid expectations of continued high ocean heat content.

events.title: Min Arctic sea ice extent this summer?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the minimum Arctic sea ice extent for all days between August 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, as published by the National Snow and Ice Data Center.

This market will remain open until data has been published for October 1, 2026, at which point it will resolve immediately. Any revisions to sea ice extent recorded after data is published for October 1, 2026 will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to thousands of square kilometers (e.g. 4.255 million sq km). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the National Snow and Ice Data Center, specifically the minimum value recorded for any day between August 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026 in the “NH-Daily-Extent” tab of the “Sea Ice Index Daily Extent” data set, available at https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/sea-ice-tools. If this resolution source becomes unavailable, another resolution source will be chosen.

eventMetadata.context_description: Record low winter maximum extent tied with 2025 at 14.29 million sq km, combined with fifth-lowest June and ninth-lowest early August extents (around 7 million sq km), anchors trader consensus around 4.4–4.6 million sq km for the September minimum. Thin first-year ice from the prior low-growth season, above-average ocean heat content in the Atlantic sector, and accelerated July melt rates (29% decline) increase vulnerability to rapid late-summer losses, while model projections cluster near 4.49 million sq km. Persistent marginal-sea deficits and variable atmospheric steering patterns create the narrow spread separating leading bins from lower-probability outcomes below 4.2 or above 4.8 million sq km, with new NSIDC and Met Office updates expected to refine positioning before peak melt.

events.title: Measles cases in U.S. in 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter (see: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) at the resolution time. If the counter becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

Note: Only cases reported by the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter will qualify, regardless of reports from U.S. State agencies or other sources.

eventMetadata.context_description: As of mid-August 2026, the CDC has confirmed 2,566 measles cases across 47 jurisdictions, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of 2,289 and marking the highest annual count since 1991. This surge stems from sustained community transmission in under-vaccinated populations, with 94% of cases linked to 38 new outbreaks and many carrying over from late-2025 clusters; 20% involve children under five. Imported cases from international travel continue seeding local spread amid global measles activity. The CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices is reviewing elimination status this month, while weekly case reports and state surveillance updates through year-end will determine final totals and any shifts in transmission dynamics.

events.title: 9.0 or above earthquake before 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if 1 or more earthquakes with a magnitude of 9.0 or higher occur anywhere on Earth between December 8, 2025 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2026, 11:59PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used. 

After a qualifying earthquake is registered, this market will remain open for 24 hours to account for any revisions to its recorded magnitude. After 24 hours, this market will resolve according to the latest provided data.

eventMetadata.context_description: The strong trader consensus against a magnitude 9.0 or greater earthquake before 2027 reflects the extreme rarity of such megaquakes, which occur on average once every decade or longer globally according to USGS historical catalogs. No subduction zone currently shows the prolonged seismic precursors, slow-slip events, or elevated strain accumulation that typically precede these events, and monitoring data through mid-2026 indicate background activity levels only. The brief remaining window further lowers odds, as even high-probability regions like the Cascadia or Japan trenches rarely produce threshold events on such short timescales. An unexpected cluster of foreshocks or revised fault models could alter this assessment if detected in coming months.

events.title: 10.0 or above earthquake before 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if 1 or more earthquakes with a magnitude of 10.0 or higher occur anywhere on Earth between December 8, 2025 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2026, 11:59PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used. 

After a qualifying earthquake is registered, this market will remain open for 24 hours to account for any revisions to its recorded magnitude. After 24 hours, this market will resolve according to the latest provided data.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Scientific consensus from the USGS and seismological data establishes that a magnitude 10.0 earthquake is physically impossible on Earth.** Earthquake magnitude scales with fault rupture length and slip; no known fault is long enough to release the required energy—roughly equivalent to a fault spanning much of the planet's circumference. The largest recorded event reached 9.5 in Chile's 1960 Valdivia quake along a ~1,000 km subduction zone, with all subsequent great events (such as the 9.2 Alaska 1964 and 9.1–9.2 Sumatra 2004) falling well below 10.0.

In the brief window remaining before 2027, recent global monitoring shows only moderate activity, with 2026 events peaking around 7.7–7.8. Market-implied odds near 99% reflect this established geophysical limit rather than forecast uncertainty, though traders recognize that any future revision in maximum-magnitude scaling laws could theoretically reopen debate.
